decisions.executionNote: Begin elbow-up approach, tipping grippers downward toward the left yellow pepper and right-side car. Geometry and tool offset are estimated from RGB.
Align vertically above yellow pepper and outer right car; finish downward wrist orientation before descending.
Lower cautiously for first grasps; refine forward alignment and rotate the right jaws across the car body.
Close and test-lift the yellow pepper. Refine car centering, lower gently, then close and begin a small retention check.
Lift both apparent grasps clear of the table, then carry yellow pepper toward the middle basket and car toward the right basket without crossing arms.
Pepper is visibly retained; carry with smaller increments and reduced height for continuity. Car remained on table, so reopen and return lower for a new grasp.
Reduce left height to stay away from the extension boundary while approaching the middle basket front. Continue cautious car descent with open jaws.
Place yellow at the front interior of the blue middle basket. Back the right arm away from possible rim/arm contact and reduce its yaw before retrying the car.
Tilt the held pepper forward over the middle basket instead of forcing the left reach boundary. Reapproach the car from farther back with restored near-vertical jaws.
Recover from the unexecuted continuity rejection with much smaller initial left pitch increments; right repeats the backed-off car approach.
Advance the tilted pepper slightly into blue and release. Lower the right car approach while shifting forward to center its body between the jaws.
Yellow is visibly in blue. Close and test-lift the right car at the contact-limited height while the left retracts toward the central chocolate bar.
Car is visibly retained; carry it inward toward red with a forward wrist tilt. Align left jaws across the central chocolate's short dimension.
Lift car clear of the basket rim before lateral carry, backing slightly away from contact. Finish left chocolate alignment and descend to grasp height.
Center and close on chocolate. Car appears to have slipped back to the table; reopen and descend vertically for a more central grasp.
Lift chocolate and start leftward transfer. Regrasp the car where it now rests near the red basket; use a short descent rather than dragging it over the rim.
Chocolate did not stay retained; reopen and reacquire at its shifted position. Raise the car straight up before any basket transfer, checking retention next.
Corrected malformed row; no preceding motion occurred. Recenter chocolate and close stationary, while returning open right jaws to the car body.
Check chocolate retention with a straight slow lift. Back the right jaws away from the basket rim and center on the car, restoring near-vertical orientation.
Chocolate remains visibly clamped; carry toward white with a gentle forward tilt. Nudge right jaws forward toward the car's central body rather than closing on its nose.
Release the retained chocolate over the white basket interior. Close on the car body and lift straight up before attempting another rim crossing.
Chocolate is in white. Lift retained car higher before crossing red's rim, and retract the left arm toward the remaining left car.
Car again slipped; use calibrated head geometry to shift the grasp rearward onto its center. Center the left car similarly and restore a vertical left wrist.
Wrist views show both car bodies forward and off-center. Visually center both at grasp depth, with left jaws turned across its diagonal body.
Right car now centered at the jaw contact region: close, pause, and lift slowly. Lift left clear before correcting alignment to avoid pushing its car.
Lift the right car straight and slowly to rim clearance without rotating it. Bring left jaws down over its car's shifted body from above.
Back away from the rims and orient jaws across the cars' current chassis. Previous car lifts were not retained; retry a body-centered grasp rather than wheel or wing contact.
Fine visual centering of the chassis within each rotated gripper, descending only a few centimeters before closing.
Close at the current centered chassis view and lift away from basket contacts. Keep orientations fixed to test real car retention.
Right car appears securely body-clamped; raise and translate inward without changing its grasp orientation. Recenter open left jaws on the other car.
Right car remains retained after the high lift; carry over red with gentle forward tilt. Center left jaws farther onto its chassis and close.
Release the securely retained right car into red. Clear the left gripper from white-rim interference and reorient before another approach.
Car is visibly inside red. Move right to the front red pepper; refine left car position inward while restoring cross-chassis jaw alignment.
Left motion is obstructed by the white rim; back up and away before repositioning. Lower and center right over the front pepper.
Close and lift the front pepper. Approach left car again with a truly vertical tool axis to reduce forward rim interference.
Carry retained red pepper toward blue. Partly narrow left jaws before forward centering near the white rim, then close on the car chassis.
Deposit red pepper inside blue. Left missed the chassis laterally; reopen above it and make a small rotated visual correction with narrowed jaws.
Two peppers are in blue. Approach the final pepper; withdraw left and change to jaws parallel to the white front rim to avoid the repeated cross-rim obstruction.
Descend to the remaining pepper and close. Lower left with the jaws parallel to the basket rim, retaining the new collision-avoiding orientation.
Lift the last pepper toward blue. Close left at the unobstructed pose, then pull back from white while testing whether the car is retained.
Place the last pepper into blue. Reorient left above the now horizontal car, using a narrower opening to approach beside the white rim.
Release pepper without further forward extension, then approach the last chocolate with right. Finish the narrowed left cross-body car approach from the current pose.
Replan the rejected right withdrawal with a gradual ramp away from extension. Visually center left on the car using the rotated wrist view and close with reduced rim clearance.
Car is still beside the left jaws, not held. Shift the half-open jaws toward its chassis while preserving rim clearance; center right vertically over the last chocolate.
Withdraw left from the rim and try a diagonal jaw orientation next. Align right jaws with the chocolate wrapper and close before transferring it through the center.
Lift the clamped chocolate toward a central handoff staging point. Bring the closed left gripper beside the car to gently displace it away from the obstructing white rim.
Stage the retained chocolate at the center-front for the left arm. Gently slide the left car laterally away from the white wall rather than repeatedly attempting the obstructed grasp.
Release chocolate at the center-front and clear the right arm. Continue sliding the car away from white toward the center without crossing the left arm into the right workspace.
Car has shifted clear of white but contact limited the push. Continue in smaller increments with a slight retreat from the rim; keep right clear of the staged chocolate.
The car stayed behind the last slide. Recenter on its now clearer location and close across its short dimension with a reduced opening, keeping right safely out of the way.
Make a small body-centering correction from the new wrist view, then close stationary. Avoid further large car pushes near the sorted baskets.
Lift before opening fully and repositioning over the car chassis; the previous narrowed approach closed beside it. Keep the right arm stationary and clear.
Use the closed left tip to slide the obstructed car laterally out of the basket gap toward the center, rather than forcing open jaws against the wall.
Recenter over the car body rather than its rear wing, correct the tool-axis tilt, and close with only the necessary opening near the rim.
The rear wing blocked the narrowed descent. Lift and fully open, approach farther toward the cockpit and slightly away from the basket wall before descending again.
Back clear of the persistent basket collision and rotate the jaws parallel to the rim. The current cross-rim approach cannot descend safely.
Approach the car with vertical fingers and jaw travel parallel to the basket front, correcting accumulated orientation error rather than repeating the obstructed side grip.
Close at the parallel-rim pose, pause, then lift backward away from the wall to check retention or at least bring the car into open workspace.
Leave the unretained car for a later approach and retrieve the chocolate staged at center-front with the left arm, staying within the left workspace.
Correct chocolate alignment rearward in the rotated wrist view without moving the left arm across the center, then close stationary.
The wrapper turned instead of being retained. Reopen above it and rotate across its new short dimension, using a left-of-center EE position.
Fine-center the staged chocolate, lower to the previously successful wrapper grasp height, and close across its short dimension.
Chocolate is centered and clamped. Lift and carry toward the left basket, checking visual retention before the final transfer.
Chocolate slipped during lateral lift. Reopen and center on the now-leftward wrapper for a central grasp, then use a straight retention lift.
Move the wrapper midpoint, rather than its end, into the jaw contact region and close. Next lift will be vertical only.
Straight vertical retention check for the chocolate, keeping the jaws closed and orientation fixed.
Chocolate remains visibly retained after the full lift. Carry it toward white with a gradual forward tilt, maintaining left-workspace clearance.
Correct malformed idle row; previous act moved nothing. Advance retained chocolate over white and release beside the earlier chocolate.
Both chocolates are now in white. Approach the remaining car with a vertical cross-body grip, accounting for the tool offset and using a half opening to clear the front rim.
Car chassis is now within the jaw region. Make a millimeter-scale centering correction, close, and settle before any lift.
Reopen clear of the car and shift the contact point from its narrow nose toward the cockpit, restoring the vertical tool orientation before descending.
Abandon the rim-blocked top grasp. Retract left and begin a low, closed-tip side approach to move the car into clear central workspace, preserving elbow-up continuity.
Move farther back from the fixed rim while completing a horizontal closed-tip approach. Replan from actual pose after the contact residual; do not force through the basket.
Keep the accepted near-horizontal orientation to avoid the wrist continuity boundary. Align the closed tip with the car's left end at table height before a gentle lateral push.
The low side approach is contact-limited. Raise the elbow-up arm and restore a steeper closed-tip angle, keeping the car approach from its left side rather than forcing lower.
No motion occurred on the rejected recovery. Rebase with stationary targets, then raise away from contact using much smaller pose increments.
Align the closed side-facing tip with the car's left end using modest descent and forward correction, stopping above the earlier contact-limited height.
Gently advance the closed side-facing tip into the car's left end to slide it rightward away from the basket gap; stop and reassess if contact causes poor tracking.
Side push is obstructed. Reconfigure to a forward-tilted top grasp with the wrist farther behind the baskets, leaving room for the forearm while the fingers reach the car.
